summary:
The paper proves the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture for Krämer models of unitary Rapoport–Zink spaces at a ramified place (p odd), for every n (Theorem 1.3). The conjecture was formulated by He–Shi–Yang. It says that the arithmetic intersection number Int(L) of n special divisors on the semistable Krämer model equals the modified derived local density ∂Den(L): the derivative Den′(L) corrected by rational multiples c_{2j} of local densities against duals of vertex lattices.

The proof follows Li–Zhang's GSpin strategy.
- Split Int and ∂Den along a rank n − 1 lattice L^♭ into horizontal and vertical parts.
- The horizontal parts agree through the n = 2 results (Theorem 9.5).
- Both vertical parts have partial Fourier transforms that are constant on W_{≥0}:
  - geometrically, via a new Bruhat–Tits stratification of the Krämer model by Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_V (Theorems 3.16, 3.19) and translation invariance of intersections with the strata (Theorem 4.14), avoiding any Tate conjecture;
  - analytically, via a closed formula for the modified derivative of primitive local densities (Theorem 7.1) and lattice-count identities (Propositions 8.7, 8.9).
- An induction on val(L^♭) finishes the proof (Theorem 9.7).
Globally, this relaxes the local hypotheses of the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula for U(n − 1, 1) to allow Krämer level at ramified places (Theorems 10.1–10.2).

The libraries have none of this. The atlas plans the Fourier transform (AL.0), K-theory with supports (S.6–S.7) and the q-binomial theorem (QM.0).

Routes:
- the geometric and global parts to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles, and the Krämer RZ spaces and RSZ models to UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels, both candidates of PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B;
- the local-density analysis to GN.3 as a source.

Theorem 7.1 was checked independently for integral lattices: Corollary 6.2 with brute-force finite-field counts reproduces it over F_3 (n ≤ 4) and F_5 (n ≤ 3).

Six source issues are recorded:
- E1 (gap): at almost self-dual inert places Theorem 10.1 relies on Li–Zhang Theorem 10.5.1, which is conditional on Li–Zhang Conjecture 10.4.1 (later proved by Li–Rapoport–Zhang);
- E2: Proposition 3.20's criterion needs L integral;
- E3–E6: misprints, one of them already corrected in the final version.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (Kudla–Rapoport conjecture for Krämer models)
items.statement: Let F/F_0 be a ramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields, p odd, π a uniformizer with Tr π = 0, N = N_n the Krämer model of signature (1, n − 1) (n ≥ 2) and V its n-dimensional hermitian space of special quasi-homomorphisms. For every O_F-lattice L ⊆ V of full rank, Int(L) = ∂Den(L), where Int(L) = χ(N, O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_n)}) for a basis x_i (Definition 1.1, independent of the basis [How19, Cor. D]), and ∂Den(L) = Den′(L) + Σ_{j=1}^{t_max/2} c_{2j}·Den_{2j}(L) (Definition 1.2), with Den′(L) = Den′(I_n, L)/Den(I_n, I_n) (I_n unimodular of sign −χ(L)), Den_t(L) = Den(Λ^♯_t, L)/Den(Λ^♯_t, Λ^♯_t) for a vertex lattice Λ_t of type t, t_max = n, n − 1, n − 2 according as n is even with χ(V) = 1, n is odd, or n is even with χ(V) = −1, and the c_{2j} ∈ Q the unique solution of ∂Den(Λ^♯_{2i}) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ t_max/2 [HSY23a, Thm. 6.1].
items.locator: Definitions 1.1–1.2, (1.1)–(1.6) and Theorem 1.3, pp.3–4; proof §9, pp.73–76, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: This proves the conjecture of He–Shi–Yang (Compositio 2023) for all n; n = 2, 3 were known. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Theorem 7.1 = Theorem 1.6 (the modified derivative of the primitive local density)
items.statement: For an O_F-lattice L ⊆ V of rank n: (1) if L is not integral, ∂Pden(L) = 0; (2) if L is unimodular, ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) = 1 for n odd and 0 for n even; (3) if L = I_{n−t} ⊥ L_2 with L_2 of full type t > 0, ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) = Π_{ℓ=1}^{(t−1)/2}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for t odd and (1 − χ(L_2)q^{t/2})Π_{ℓ=1}^{t/2−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for t even. Here ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) + Σ_j c_{2j}Pden_{2j}(L) is the primitive analogue of ∂Den, so ∂Den(L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L_F} ∂Pden(L′) (1.13).
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p.8; Theorem 7.1 and proof §7.6, pp.46, 62–64, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Checked independently for (2)–(3): Corollary 6.2 with brute-force counts of Σ_{V_1} |O(V_1, Ī_n)| over F_3 (n ≤ 4, 40 cases) and F_5 (n ≤ 3) reproduces every value; the non-integral cases H^j ⊥ L_1 with t(L_1) > 0 give Pden(I_n, L_1, q^{2j}) = 0 as in §7.6. Statement (3) omits t > 0, stated in Theorem 1.6 (sourceIssues E3). Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Corollaries 7.2–7.3 and Lemma 7.4 (integrality and the analytic cancellation law)
items.statement: ∂Den(L) ∈ Z for every L, and ∂Den(L) = 0 for non-integral L. For L = L_1 ⊥ L_2 with L_1 unimodular of rank n_1 and L_2 of rank n_2: ∂Den(L) − ∂Den(L_2) = n(I_{n_2}, L_2)·(δ_odd(n) − δ_odd(n_2)) (7.3), where n(L′, L) counts lattices L″ ⊇ L in L_F isometric to L′. Lemma 7.4: if L ⊊ L′ ⊆ π^{−1}L and L′ is not of the form L_1 ⊥ L′_2, then L′ is not integral.
items.locator: Corollaries 7.2–7.3 and Lemma 7.4, pp.46–47, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Formal hermitian O_F-modules and the Krämer model N_n (Definitions 2.1–2.2)
items.statement: A formal hermitian O_F-module of dimension n over S ∈ Nilp_{O_F̆} is (X, ι, λ): a supersingular strict O_{F_0}-module of dimension n and F_0-height 2n, an O_F-action ι, and a principal polarization λ whose Rosati involution is Galois conjugation on O_F. N_n(S) classifies (X, ι, λ, ρ, 𝓕) with ρ a height-zero quasi-isogeny to a fixed framing object of signature (1, n − 1) and 𝓕 ⊆ Lie X a rank n − 1 local direct summand on which O_F acts through ī, with O_F acting on Lie X/𝓕 through i (Krämer's condition [Krä03]). N_n is a relative RZ space in the sense of [Mih22], representable by a flat formal scheme of relative dimension n − 1 over Spf O_F̆ [How19, Prop. 2.2], regular and semistable; the two framing objects give non-isomorphic spaces for n even and isomorphic ones for n odd.
items.locator: Definitions 2.1–2.2, §§1.2, 2.1–2.2, pp.2, 10–11, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The hermitian spaces C and V = Hom_{O_F}(𝕐, 𝕏) ⊗ Q
items.statement: On the rational relative Dieudonné module N of 𝕏, (x, y) := δ(⟨Πx, y⟩ + π⟨x, y⟩) (2.1) with σ(δ) = −δ, recovering ⟨x, y⟩ = (1/2δ)Tr(π^{−1}(x, y)) (2.2); C = N^{τ}, τ = ΠV^{−1}, an n-dimensional F/F_0-hermitian space whose sign χ(C) = χ((−1)^{n(n−1)/2} det C) distinguishes the framing objects. For the signature (0, 1) object 𝕐, V = Hom_{O_F}(𝕐, 𝕏) ⊗ Q with (x, y)_V = λ_𝕐^{−1} ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ_𝕏 ∘ x (2.4), and b : V → C, x ↦ x(e), is an isometry after scaling λ_𝕐 ((2.5)–(2.6), [Shi18, Lemma 3.6]).
items.locator: §2.2, (2.1)–(2.6), pp.10–12, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Special cycles Z(L) and the canonical lift (Definition 2.3)
items.statement: With a canonical lift 𝒢 of 𝕐 to O_F̆ (unique by [How19, Prop. 2.1], O_F acting on Lie 𝒢 through ī), Z(L) ⊆ N for L ⊆ V is the closed formal subscheme where ρ^{−1} ∘ x ∘ ρ_𝒢 lifts to a homomorphism 𝒢 × S → X for every x ∈ L (Grothendieck–Messing); Z(x) = Z(⟨x⟩) is a Cartier divisor [How19, Prop. 4.3].
items.locator: Definition 2.3, §2.3, p.12; §2.6, p.14, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Definition 2.4 and Lemma 2.5 (the exceptional divisor)
items.statement: Exc ⊆ N(κ̄) is the locus where O_F acts on Lie X through O_F → O_F̆ → κ̄; Exc_Λ (Λ a type-0 vertex lattice of C) is the part with ρ(M(X)) = Λ ⊗ O_F̆. Each Exc_Λ is a Cartier divisor of N isomorphic to P^{n−1}_κ̄, and Exc is their disjoint union (refining [How19, Prop. A.2]; agreeing with [HSY23a, §2]).
items.locator: Definition 2.4, Lemma 2.5, Remark 2.6, pp.12–13, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Horizontal and vertical parts; Lemmas 2.7–2.8
items.statement: For a formal scheme 𝒳 over Spf O_F̆, 𝒳_H is defined by the torsion ideal and, when 𝒳 is noetherian with π^m killing torsion, 𝒳_V by π^m O_𝒳, so 𝒳 = 𝒳_H ∪ 𝒳_V (2.8). For L^♭ ⊆ V of rank ≥ n − 1 non-degenerate, Z(L^♭) is noetherian (Lemma 2.7), and for rank n − 1, Z(L^♭)_V is supported on N_red, the supersingular locus (Lemma 2.8, as [LZ22a, Lemma 5.1.1]).
items.locator: §2.5, (2.8), Lemmas 2.7–2.8, pp.13–14, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Proposition 2.12 (geometric cancellation law)
items.statement: For L = I_ℓ ⊥ L_2 ⊆ V with I_ℓ unimodular of rank ℓ, L_2 of rank r, n = ℓ + r, and I_r ⊇ L_2 unimodular: Int(I_ℓ ⊥ L_2) − Int(L_2) = n(I_r, L_2)·(δ_odd(n) − δ_odd(r)) (2.12), and Int(I_n) = δ_odd(n) (2.13). Proof: Z(I_1) = Z̃(I_1) + Σ_{Λ_0 ⊇ I_1} Exc_{Λ_0} with Z̃(I_1) ≅ N_{n−1} [HSY23a, Prop. 3.2, Cor. 2.7], χ([O_{Exc_{Λ_0}}]·^𝕃Z(L_2)) = (−1)^r [HSY23a, Cor. 3.6], and Int(L_2) = 0 for L_2 unimodular of rank 2 [Shi22, Thm. 1.3; HSY23b, Thm. 1.3].
items.locator: Proposition 2.12 and proof, (2.12)–(2.15), p.15, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: The telescoping from (2.14) to (2.12) was checked. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The Deligne–Lusztig varieties S_V and Y_V (§3.1)
items.statement: For a 2m-dimensional symplectic F_q-space V: S_V = {U ∈ SGr(m, V) : dim(U ∩ Φ(U)) ≥ m − 1} (3.1), irreducible of dimension m with isolated singularities exactly at U = Φ(U) [RTW14, Props. 5.3, 5.5]; Y_V = {(U, U′) : U′ ⊆ U ∩ Φ(U)} ⊆ SGr(m, V) × SGr(m − 1, V) (3.2). Lemma 3.1: Y_V → S_V is projective, an isomorphism off the singular locus, with fibres P^{m−1} over singular points. Proposition 3.2: Y_V is irreducible and smooth projective of dimension m (a transversal intersection, Φ inducing zero on tangent spaces). Remark 3.3: Y_V is the blow-up of S_V along its singular locus (stated without proof).
items.locator: §3.1, (3.1)–(3.2), Lemma 3.1, Proposition 3.2, Remark 3.3, pp.16–17, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 3.4, Proposition 3.5 and Corollary 3.6 (the minuscule cycles N_Λ and their points)
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ ⊆ V (πΛ^♯ ⊆ Λ ⊆ Λ^♯) of type t(Λ) = dim Λ^♯/Λ = 2m (even by [RTW14, Lemma 3.2]), N_Λ ⊆ Z(Λ) adds the condition x_*(Lie 𝒢) ⊆ 𝓕 for x ∈ Λ when m ≥ 1. N_red(κ̄) is in bijection with pairs of O_F̆-lattices (M, M′) in N with M^♯ = M, ΠM ⊆ τ^{−1}(M) ⊆ Π^{−1}M, VM ⊆ M′ ⊆ τ^{−1}(M) ∩ M, length(M/M′) = 1; N_Λ(κ̄) corresponds to M = Λ̆ if t(Λ) = 0 and to Λ̆ ⊆ M′ ⊆ M if t(Λ) ≥ 2.
items.locator: Definition 3.4, Proposition 3.5, (3.3), Corollary 3.6, pp.17–18, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Footnote 2: the vertex lattice Λ of [RTW14, HSY23a, HSY23b] is Λ^♯ here. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 3.7, Lemmas 3.8–3.9, Propositions 3.10 and 3.12, Corollary 3.11 (deformations of N_Λ)
items.statement: Using O_{F_0}-relative Dieudonné crystals [ACZ16] and Grothendieck–Messing theory ([How19, §3], valid for general F_0): points of Z(Λ)_z over O ∈ 𝒞 correspond to lifts (F̃^⊥, Fil̃) with Fil̃ isotropic of rank n, (Π + π)F̃^⊥ = 0, (Π − π)Fil̃ ⊆ F̃^⊥ and Fil̃ ⊇ (Π + π)Λ_{M,O}; N_Λ,z adds F̃^⊥ ⊆ Λ^⊥_{M,O} (Lemma 3.8). Z(Λ), hence N_Λ, has no O_F̆/(π²)-point (Proposition 3.10, Corollary 3.11); for Λ of type 2m ≥ 2 the tangent space of N_{Λ,κ̄} at any point has dimension ≤ m (Proposition 3.12, via [Krä03, (4.5)–(4.10)]).
items.locator: Definition 3.7, Lemmas 3.8–3.9, Proposition 3.10, Corollary 3.11, Proposition 3.12, pp.18–23, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Lemmas 3.13–3.15 and Theorem 3.16 (N_Λ ≅ Y_V)
items.statement: For Λ of type 2m ≥ 2 and V = Λ^♯/Λ with ⟨x̄, ȳ⟩_V = π_0δ⟨x, y⟩ mod π: N_{Λ,κ̄} is representable by a projective scheme and N_{Λ,κ̄} → N is a closed immersion (Lemma 3.13, as [VW11, Lemma 3.2]); U(X) = D(ρ̃_{X,+})^{−1}(Fil)/Im D(ρ_Λ) is Lagrangian of rank m (Lemma 3.14); ϕ : (X, …) ↦ (U(X), F(X)) is a bijection N_Λ(κ̄) → Y_V(κ̄) (Lemma 3.15). Theorem 3.16: N_Λ is reduced and ϕ is an isomorphism N_Λ ≅ Y_{V,κ̄}, smooth projective of dimension m (Zariski's main theorem, Proposition 3.12, [RTZ13, Lemma 10.3], Corollary 3.11).
items.locator: Lemmas 3.13–3.15 and Theorem 3.16, pp.23–25, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Proposition 3.17, Lemma 3.18, Theorem 3.19 and Proposition 3.20 (Bruhat–Tits stratification)
items.statement: For Λ_0 of type 0, N_{Λ_0} = Exc_{Λ_0} ≅ P^{n−1} (Proposition 3.17). Every (M, 𝓕) has a unique maximal vertex lattice Λ(M) ⊆ M (Lemma 3.18, [RTW14, Prop. 4.1]). Theorem 3.19: N_red = ⋃_Λ N_Λ over vertex lattices; N_{Λ′} ⊆ N_Λ if Λ ⊆ Λ′; for types ≥ 2, N_{Λ′} ∩ N_Λ ≠ ∅ iff Λ + Λ′ is a vertex lattice, and then equals N_{Λ+Λ′}; distinct type-0 strata are disjoint; N_Λ ∩ N_{Λ_0} ≠ ∅ iff Λ ⊆ Λ_0, and then ≅ P^{m−1}. Proposition 3.20: for L of rank r, Z(L)_red = ⋃_{L ⊆ Λ} N_Λ (3.18), and for integral L, Z(L) ∩ N_Λ ≠ ∅ iff L ⊆ Λ^♯ (for non-integral L the intersection is empty).
items.locator: Proposition 3.17, Lemma 3.18, Theorem 3.19, Proposition 3.20, pp.25–27, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2 and (4.1) (horizontal lattices)
items.statement: An integral rank n − 1 lattice L^♭ ⊆ V is horizontal if it is unimodular, or L^♭ = M ⊥ L′ with M unimodular of rank n − 2 and (M_F)^⊥ nonsplit; L^♭ is horizontal iff exactly one vertex lattice contains it, which then has type 0 (Lemma 4.2, via [Shi18, Thm. 3.10] and [HSY23b, Cor. 3.11]). Hor(L^♭) = {M^♭ ∈ Hor : L^♭ ⊆ M^♭} (4.1).
items.locator: Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, (4.1), p.27, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The primitive horizontal cycles Z̃(M^♭)° and Theorem 4.3
items.statement: For dim V = 2: Z̃(y)° = Z^+_{val(y)} ⊔ Z^−_{val(y)} (quasi-canonical lifting cycles ≅ Spf W_s of degree q^s [Shi22, §3]) if χ(V) = −1 and val(y) > 0, Z_0 ≅ Spf O_F̆ if val(y) = 0, and Z^h(y) ≅ Spf O_F̆ [HSY23b, Thm. 4.1] if χ(V) = 1, val(y) = 0; for M^♭ = M ⊥ ⟨y⟩ ∈ Hor, Z̃(M^♭)° is the image of Z̃(y)° under N_2 → N_n induced by M [HSY23a, Prop. 2.6], independent of M. Theorem 4.3 [HSY23a, Thm. 4.2]: for integral non-degenerate L^♭ of rank n − 1, Z(L^♭)_H = ⋃_{M^♭ ∈ Hor(L^♭)} Z̃(M^♭)°, of pure dimension 1, and [O_{Z(L^♭)_H}] = Σ [O_{Z̃(M^♭)°}] in Gr^{n−1}K^{Z(L^♭)}_0(N).
items.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.3, (4.2)–(4.3), p.28, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Lemma 4.4, (4.4)–(4.6), Definitions 4.5 and 4.7, Lemmas 4.8–4.9 (modified horizontal and vertical parts)
items.statement: F^iK^Z_0(N) is an ideal of K_0(N) (Lemma 4.4), and Gr′K^Z_0(N) = K^Z_0(N)/F^nK^Z_0(N) (4.4) splits as Gr′K^{Z(L^♭)_H}_0 ⊕ Gr′K^{Z(L^♭)_V}_0 (4.5), giving ^𝕃Z(L^♭) = ^𝕃Z(L^♭)_H + ^𝕃Z(L^♭)_V (4.6) canonically. For horizontal L^♭, ^𝕃Z(L^♭)° = [O_{Z̃(L^♭)°}] + ((1 − (−1)^{n−1})/2)[O_{P_Λ}] if L^♭ is unimodular and [O_{Z̃(L^♭)°}] + [O_{P_Λ}] otherwise (P_Λ a line in Exc_Λ; = the difference cycle D(L^♭) of [HSY23a, Def. 2.15]). ^𝕃Z(L^♭)^*_H = Σ_{M^♭ ∈ Hor(L^♭)} ^𝕃Z(M^♭)°, ^𝕃Z(L^♭)^*_V = ^𝕃Z(L^♭) − ^𝕃Z(L^♭)^*_H ∈ Gr′K^{Z(L^♭)_V}_0(N) (Lemma 4.8), and Int_{L^♭,H/V}(x) = χ(N, ^𝕃Z(L^♭)^*_{H/V}·[O_{Z(x)}]) (4.7). Lemma 4.9: for horizontal L^♭, ^𝕃Z(L^♭)^*_H = ^𝕃Z(L^♭), by comparing intersections with N_Λ ([HSY23a, Lemma 4.4, Cors. 3.5–3.7]).
items.locator: Lemma 4.4, (4.4)–(4.7), Definitions 4.5, 4.7, Remark 4.6, Lemmas 4.8–4.9, pp.28–30, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: (4.9) m′ = m − 1 + (1 − (−1)^{n−1})/2 was rechecked from 2m − 1 − 2m′ = (−1)^{n−1}. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The Fourier transform on V, (4.10), and Lemmas 4.10–4.11
items.statement: φ̂(x) = ∫_V φ(y)ψ(Tr_{F/F_0}(x, y))dμ(y) for ψ of conductor O_{F_0} and the self-dual measure; for a lattice L with trace-dual L^∨, 1̂_L = vol(L)·1_{L^∨} (Lemma 4.10); φ is L-invariant iff φ̂ is supported on L^∨ (Lemma 4.11).
items.locator: §4.2, (4.10), Lemmas 4.10–4.11, pp.30–31, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: AL.0 plans local Fourier transforms, self-dual measures and inversion; these two lemmas are its first consequences.

items.name: Definition 4.12, Lemma 4.13 and Theorems 4.14–4.16 (the geometric side under Fourier transform)
items.statement: S(V)_{≥m} = {φ : φ̂ supported on V_{≥m}}; every Λ-invariant function for a vertex lattice Λ lies in S(V)_{≥−1}, since Λ^∨ = π^{−1}Λ^♯ ⊆ V_{≥−1} (Lemma 4.13). Theorem 4.14: for K ∈ K^{N_Λ}_0(N), x ↦ K·[O_{Z(x)}] is Λ-invariant (K·[O_{Z(x)}] = K·[O_{Z(x+y)}] for y ∈ Λ, by [How19, Cor. C] and N_Λ ⊆ Z(y)), and Int_K(x) = χ(K·[O_{Z(x)}]) extends to a Λ-invariant function in S(V)_{≥−1}. Theorem 4.15: Int_{L^♭,V} extends to an element of S(V)_{≥−1}. Theorem 4.16: the partial Fourier transform Int^⊥_{L^♭,V}(x) = ∫_{L^♭_F} Int_{L^♭,V}(x + y)dy (4.12) lies in S(W)_{≥−1} and is W_{≥0}-invariant, W = (L^♭_F)^⊥; in particular it is constant on W_{≥0}.
items.locator: Definition 4.12, Lemma 4.13, Theorems 4.14–4.16, (4.11)–(4.12), pp.31–32, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: No Tate conjecture for the Deligne–Lusztig strata is needed, unlike the unramified case (Lemma 4.13 already controls the Fourier support). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 5.1, (5.1)–(5.5) (local densities, primitive local densities and their derivatives)
items.statement: For hermitian lattices M, L of ranks m, n: Den(M, L) = lim_d |Herm_{L,M}(O_{F_0}/π_0^{d+a})|/q^{2(d+a)nm−dn²}; Den(M, L, X) ∈ Q[X] with Den(M, L, q^{−2k}) = Den(M ⊥ H^k, L) (5.1), H the hyperbolic plane with matrix [[0, π^{−1}], [−π^{−1}, 0]]; Den′(M, L) = −2(d/dX)Den(M, L, X)|_{X=1} (5.2); the primitive version Pden(M, L, X) counting primitive ϕ (dim of the image of L in (M ⊥ H^k)/π(M ⊥ H^k) equal to n) (5.3); Pden′(L), Pden_t(L) (5.4) and ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) + Σ c_{2j}Pden_{2j}(L) (5.5). Den(M, L) = 0 for M, L of rank n with χ(M) = −χ(L) (Lemma 5.7). Normal bases and fundamental invariants follow [LL22, Def. 2.11, Lemma 2.12] (§1.5).
items.locator: Definition 5.1, (5.1)–(5.5), p.33; §1.5, p.9, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (vanishing for very non-integral lattices)
items.statement: If some x ∈ L has val(x) ≤ −1, then ∂Den(L) = Den′(L) = ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) = 0, since I_n, Λ^♯_t and H^k contain no vector of valuation ≤ −1.
items.locator: Lemma 5.2, p.33, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.3, Corollary 5.4, Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 5.6 (primitive decomposition)
items.statement: Den(M, L, X) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L_F} (q^{n−m}X)^{ℓ(L′/L)} Pden(M, L′, X), a finite sum [HSY23a, Lemma 5.1]; hence ∂Den(L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′} ∂Pden(L′) (Corollary 5.4). Conversely Pden(M, L, X) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2 + i(n−m)} X^i Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ π^{−1}L, ℓ(L′/L) = i} Den(M, L′, X) [HSY23a, Thm. 5.2], so ∂Pden(L) = Σ_i (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} Σ_{ℓ(L′/L) = i} ∂Den(L′) (Corollary 5.6).
items.locator: Lemma 5.3, Corollary 5.4, Theorem 5.5, Corollary 5.6, p.34, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.7, Corollaries 5.8–5.10, Example 5.11 and (5.8) (the coefficients c_t)
items.statement: For M, L of the same rank, Pden(M, L) = Den(M, L) if M ≅ L and 0 otherwise, and Den(M, L) = n(M, L)·Den(M, M); so Den_t(L) ∈ Z (Corollary 5.8), ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) unless L ≅ Λ^♯_t with t > 0 (Corollary 5.9), and c_t = −Pden′(Λ^♯_t) (Corollary 5.10), computed from Lemma 5.13 and Corollary 6.2. Example 5.11: c_{t_max} = (−1)^{(n+1)/2}/(q^{((n−1)/2)²}(q^{(n−1)/2} + 1)) for n odd and (−1)^{n/2}/(q^{(n/2)(n/2−1)}(q^{n/2} + 1)) for n even with ϵ = 1, with a table for n ≤ 6; the closed formula (5.8) is stated as observed but not proved.
items.locator: Lemma 5.7, Corollaries 5.8–5.10, Example 5.11 and (5.8), pp.34–36, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: The table agrees with (5.7) and (5.8) in every listed entry; c_2 for n = 2, 3, 4 at q = 3 was also recomputed from Corollary 6.2 with brute-force counts. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 5.12–5.13 (hyperbolic summands)
items.statement: For integral L of rank n, Pden(H^k, L) = Π_{ℓ=0}^{n−1}(1 − q^{−2k+2ℓ}) (from [LL22, Lemma 2.15]). For L = H^j ⊥ L_1 (j > 0, L_1 integral of rank n_1): Den(I_m, L, X) = Π_{ℓ=0}^{j−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ}X)·Den(I_m, L_1, q^{2j}X), the same for Pden, and Pden′(I_m, L) = 2Π_{ℓ=1}^{j−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ})·Pden(I_m, L_1, q^{2j}) (5.9) (from [HSY23a, Cor. 5.8]).
items.locator: Lemmas 5.12–5.13, (5.9)–(5.10), pp.36–37, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definitions 5.14–5.15, Lemma 5.16 and Corollary 5.17 (densities as finite-field isometry counts)
items.statement: O(U, V) is the set of isometries of quadratic spaces over F_q from U into V and M(U, V) the set of subspaces isometric to U, m(U, V) = |M(U, V)|; U^ϵ_i is the non-degenerate i-dimensional space of sign ϵ and 0_i the totally isotropic one. For L = I^{ϵ_1}_{n−t} ⊥ L_2 with L_2 of full type t and n ≤ m: Pden(I^{ϵ_2}_m, L) = q^{−mn+n²}·|O(0_t ⊥ U^{ϵ_1}_{n−t}, U^{ϵ_2}_m)| [HSY23a, Lemma A.11], with the explicit count of |O(0_j ⊥ U^{ϵ_1}_k, U^ϵ_m)| from [LZ22b, Lemma 3.2.1]; Den(I_n, I_n) = 2q^{n(n−1)/2}Π_{s=1}^{(n−1)/2}(1 − q^{−2s}) for n odd and 2q^{n(n−1)/2}(1 + ϵq^{−n/2})Π_{s=1}^{n/2−1}(1 − q^{−2s}) for n even (I_n of sign −ϵ).
items.locator: Definitions 5.14–5.15, Lemma 5.16, Corollary 5.17, p.37, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Corollary 5.17 agrees with the orders of the finite orthogonal groups, and with (7.8). Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 5.18–5.19, Corollary 5.20 and Lemmas 5.21–5.22 (counting subspaces of quadratic spaces over F_q)
items.statement: m(0_j ⊥ U^{ϵ_2}_k, U^ϵ_n) = |O(0_j ⊥ U^{ϵ_2}_k, U^ϵ_n)|/(q^{jk}|O(U^{ϵ_2}_k)|·|GL_j(F_q)|) = q^{−jk}m(0_j, U^{δ(n,k,ϵ,ϵ_2)}_{n−k})·m(U^{ϵ_2}_k, U^ϵ_n) with δ as in (5.12) (Lemma 5.18, Witt's theorem); m(0_j ⊥ U^{ϵ_2}_k, 0_t ⊥ U^{ϵ_1}_{n−t}) = Σ_{ℓ ≤ min(t,j)} [t choose ℓ]_q q^{(t−ℓ)(j+k−ℓ)} m(0_{j−ℓ} ⊥ U^{ϵ_2}_k, U^{ϵ_1}_{n−t}) (Lemma 5.19) and the resulting isometry count (Corollary 5.20); the ratios m(U^{−ϵ_1}_r, U^ϵ_n)/m(U^{ϵ_1}_r, U^ϵ_n) and m(U^{ϵ_1}_{r+1}, U^ϵ_n)/m(U^{ϵ_1}_r, U^ϵ_n) (Lemma 5.21); and the flag identity m(U^σ_i, U^ϵ_n)m(U^{δ(r,i,δ′,σ)}_{r−i}, U^{δ(n,i,ϵ,σ)}_{n−i}) = m(U^{δ′}_r, U^ϵ_n)m(U^σ_i, U^{δ′}_r) (Lemma 5.22).
items.locator: §5.3, (5.11)–(5.12), Lemmas 5.18–5.22, Corollary 5.20, pp.37–39, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 5.23 and Lemma 5.24 (Gaussian binomial coefficients and the q-binomial theorem)
items.statement: [n choose i]_q = (q^n − 1)⋯(q^{n−i+1} − 1)/((q^i − 1)⋯(q − 1)), the number of i-dimensional subspaces of F_q^n; Π_{i=0}^{n−1}(1 − q^iX) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}[n choose i]_q X^i (5.13).
items.locator: Definition 5.23, Lemma 5.24, (5.13), pp.39–40, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: QM.0 plans q-binomial identities in formal power-series rings.

items.name: Corollary 5.25 and Lemma 5.26 (consequences of the q-binomial theorem)
items.statement: For f of degree ≤ n − 1, Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}[n choose i]_q f(q^{−i}) = 0; and Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}[n choose i]_q Π_{ℓ=0}^{i−1}(1 + q^{−ℓ}X) = (−X)^n (by the recursion (5.14) in the basis g_i(X) = Π_{ℓ<i}(1 + q^{−ℓ}X)).
items.locator: Corollary 5.25, Lemma 5.26, (5.14), p.40, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 6.1, Corollaries 6.2–6.3 and Lemmas 6.4–6.6 (decomposition of primitive local densities)
items.statement: For L integral of rank n and m ≥ 0: Pden(I_m, L, X) = Σ_{i=0}^n Pden_{n−i}(I_m, L, X) with Pden_{n−i}(I_m, L, q^{−2k}) = q^{−2ki}Pden(H^k, 0_{n−i})Σ_{V_1 ∈ Gr(i, L̄)} q^{(n−i)i}Pden(I_m, L_{V_1}) (6.1), by sorting primitive embeddings by the rank of their projection to H^k; hence Pden(I_m, L, X) = Σ_i (q^{n−m}X)^i Π_{ℓ=0}^{n−i−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ}X)·Σ_{V_1 ∈ Gr(i, L̄)}|O(V_1, Ī_m)| (6.2) and Pden′(I_n, L) = 2Σ_i Π_{ℓ=1}^{n−i−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ})Σ_{V_1}|O(V_1, Ī_n)| (Corollary 6.2), and for L of full type the inner sum is [n choose i]_q|O(0_i, Ī_m)| (Corollary 6.3). Lemmas 6.4–6.6: primitive embeddings into I_m ⊥ H^k with full-rank projection to H^k, moving a primitive integral image into H^k by U(I_m ⊥ H^k), and counting solutions w ∈ πH^k/π_0^dH^k of (N, w) ≡ 0 mod π^{2d−1}.
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, (6.1)–(6.13), Corollaries 6.2–6.3, Lemmas 6.4–6.6, pp.41–45, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Lemma 6.4 cites [LL22, Lemma 2.16] for [LL22, Lemma 2.15] (sourceIssues E4). Corollary 6.2 is the formula used in the numerical check of Theorem 7.1. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Propositions 7.5–7.6 (full-type and hyperbolic-plus-full-type lattices)
items.statement: If L = H^j ⊥ L_2 with j > 0 and L_2 of full type of rank n − 2j, then ∂Pden(L) = 0 (Pden(I_n, L_2, q^{n−n_2}) = 0 by Corollary 5.25 applied to g(n_2, X) of (7.7)). If L is of full type of rank n, Pden′(L) = Π_{ℓ=1}^{(n−1)/2}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for n odd and (1 − ϵq^{n/2})Π_{ℓ=1}^{n/2−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ}) for n even.
items.locator: Propositions 7.5–7.6, (7.7)–(7.8), pp.48–50, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Both are special cases of Theorem 7.1 and are covered by the numerical check there. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 7.7–7.9 (orthogonal counts as values of the polynomials f_ϵ; a q-Pascal expansion; an alternating sum)
items.statement: With f_{ϵ_2}(n, s, X) of (7.10)–(7.11) (degree n − 1) and I_ϵ(n), I_ϵ(n′, n): Π_{ℓ=1}^{n−i−1}(1 − q^{2ℓ})|O(0_{i−s} ⊥ U^{ϵ_2}_s, U^{−ϵ}_n)| = (−1)^{n−i−1}q^{i(i−1)/2}I_ϵ(n)f_{ϵ_2}(n, s, q^{−i}) and its shifted variant (Lemma 7.7); [t choose i]_q = Σ_a (−1)^a q^{a(t+1−i)}q^{a(a−1)/2}[n−t choose a]_q[n−a choose i−a]_q (7.12) (Lemma 7.8, by lattice paths); Σ_j (−1)^j q^{j(j−1)/2} m(0_j, U^ϵ_n) = α(n)β_ϵ(n), α(n) = q^{⌊n/2⌋⌊(n−1)/2⌋} (Lemma 7.9, via [LZ22b, Lemma 3.2.2] and Lemma 5.26).
items.locator: Lemmas 7.7–7.9, (7.10)–(7.13), pp.50–52, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 7.10 and Lemmas 7.11–7.13 (the polynomials g_ϵ(n, m, r, X))
items.statement: g_{ϵ_1}(n, m, r, X) = Σ_k (−1)^k q^{k(k−1)/2} Σ_{ϵ_2} m(U^{ϵ_2}_k, U^{ϵ_1}_m) Σ_j (−1)^j q^{j(j−1)/2}[m−j−k choose r−j−k]_q m(0_j, U^δ_{m−k}) f_{ϵ_2}(n, k, X) (Definition 7.10). For L of rank n and type t, m = n − t and m(n, t) = min{n − t, n − 1}: (Pden_{n−i})′(I_n, L) = 2I_ϵ(n)Σ_{r ≤ m(n,t)} [n−r choose i−r]_q (−1)^{i−r+n−1}q^{(i−r)(i−r−1)/2}q^{r(n−m)}g_{ϵ_1}(n, m, r, q^{−i}), with a shifted version at q^{n′−n} (Lemma 7.11); the identity (7.15) (Lemma 7.12); and g_{ϵ_1}(m, r, X) = Σ_{ϵ_3} m(U^{ϵ_3}_r, U^{ϵ_1}_m)g_{ϵ_3}(r, r, X) (Lemma 7.13).
items.locator: Definition 7.10, Lemmas 7.11–7.13, (7.14)–(7.18), pp.52–55, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.locator: Lemmas 7.14–7.16, (7.19)–(7.38), pp.56–62, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: The two identities of Lemma 7.14 were verified symbolically for n ≤ 7. Lemmas 7.15–7.16 prove one parity case in detail and leave the others to the reader; their consequence, Theorem 7.1, was checked numerically. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: (8.3)–(8.4), Definitions 8.3 and 8.5, Lemmas 8.4, 8.6, 8.8 and Propositions 8.7, 8.9 (the μ-invariants of full-type lattices)
items.statement: For L of full type t: μ_+(L) = |(πL^♯)°°/L|, μ_0(L) = |((πL^♯)° − (πL^♯)°°)/L|, μ_−(L) = |((L^♯)° − (πL^♯)°)/L| and μ_{0,ν} by the sign of (u, u) (L° = {val ≥ 0}, L°° = {val > 0}); μ_+ + μ_0 + μ_− = q^tμ_+ (Lemma 8.4). For non-maximal L there is L ⊆ L′ ⊆ π^{−1}L with μ_+(L, L′) + μ_0(L, L′) = qμ_+(L, L′) (Lemma 8.6) and μ_{0,+}(L, L′) = μ_{0,−}(L, L′) (Lemma 8.8). Proposition 8.7 (t odd): (1 − χq^{(t+1)/2})(1 + χq^{(t−1)/2})μ_+(L) + (1 + χq^{(t−1)/2})μ_0(L) + μ_−(L) = 0; Proposition 8.9 (t even): (1 − q^t)μ_+(L) + (1 − χq^{t/2})μ_{0,+1}(L) + (1 + χq^{t/2})μ_{0,−1}(L) + μ_−(L) = 0, both by induction on val(L) from the maximal lattices.
items.locator: (8.3)–(8.10), Definitions 8.3, 8.5, Lemmas 8.4, 8.6, 8.8, Propositions 8.7, 8.9, pp.65–73, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: The maximal-lattice evaluations in Propositions 8.7 and 8.9 were rechecked: (1 − qa)(1 + a) + (1 + a)(q − 1) + q^t − q = 0 with a² = q^{t−1}. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 9.6 (reducing the valuation of L^♭)
items.statement: For L^♭ ⊆ V non-degenerate of rank n − 1 and x ∉ L^♭ ⊥ W, there are L′^♭ of rank n − 1 and x′ with val(L′^♭) < val(L^♭) and L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ = L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ (via minors of the moment matrix, [LL22, Lemma 2.23]); analogue of [LZ22b, Lemma 9.3.1].
items.locator: Lemma 9.6 and proof, pp.74–75, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.2 (the analytic side under partial Fourier transform)
items.statement: ∂Den_{L^♭,V}(x) = Σ_{L^♭ ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^♯, L′^♭ ∉ Hor(L^♭)} ∂Pden(L′)1_{L′}(x), L′^♭ = L′ ∩ L^♭_F. Theorem 8.2: ∂Den^⊥_{L^♭,V}(x) = ∫_{L^♭_F} ∂Den_{L^♭,V}(x + y)dy is constant on W_{≥0} \ {0} and zero on W_{<0}. Proof: ∂Den^⊥(x) − ∂Den^⊥(π^{−1}x) = Σ vol(L′^♭)D(L′^♭)(x) (8.1) with D(L′^♭)(x) = Σ_{u^♭ ∈ (L′^♭)^♯/L′^♭, val(u^♭) ≥ 0} ∂Pden(L′^♭ + ⟨u^♭ + x⟩) (8.2), which vanishes by Theorem 7.1 and Propositions 8.7 and 8.9 ((8.5)–(8.6)), using [LZ22a, Lemmas 7.2.1–7.2.2].
items.locator: Definition 8.1, Theorem 8.2 and proof, (8.1)–(8.6), pp.64–67, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 9.1, Definition 9.2, Lemmas 9.3–9.4 and Theorem 9.5 (the horizontal identity)
items.statement: For L = L_1 ⊥ L_2 with L_1 unimodular, Int(L) − ∂Den(L) = Int(L_2) − ∂Den(L_2) (from (2.12) and (7.3)). With ∂Den_{L^♭,H}(x) = Σ_{L′^♭ ∈ Hor(L^♭)} ∂Pden(L′)1_{L′}(x) (9.1): for horizontal L^♭, Int_{L^♭,H} = ∂Den_{L^♭,H} (Lemma 9.3, from n = 2 [Shi22, Thm. 1.1; HSY23b, Thm. 1.1] and Lemma 9.1); for horizontal M^♭, χ(N, ^𝕃Z(M^♭)°·Z(x)) = Σ_{L′^♭ = M^♭} ∂Pden(L′)1_{L′}(x) (Lemma 9.4, induction on val(M^♭)); and Int_{L^♭,H} = ∂Den_{L^♭,H} for every non-degenerate L^♭ of rank n − 1 (Theorem 9.5).
items.locator: Lemma 9.1, Definition 9.2, Lemmas 9.3–9.4, Theorem 9.5, pp.73–74, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Theorem 9.7 and Corollary 9.8 (conclusion of the proof)
items.statement: For non-degenerate L^♭ of rank n − 1 and x ∈ V \ L^♭_F, Int_{L^♭}(x) = ∂Den_{L^♭}(x), which gives Theorem 1.3. Proof by induction on val(L^♭): non-integral L^♭ gives 0 = 0 (Proposition 3.20, Corollary 7.2); by Lemma 9.6 the difference Φ_{L^♭} is supported on L^♭ ⊥ W and equals 1_{L^♭} ⊗ ϕ_W; Theorem 9.5 leaves only the vertical parts; ϕ_W vanishes on W_{≤0} (Lemma 9.1 and induction on rank for val = 0, non-integrality for val < 0), and Theorems 4.16 and 8.2 make Φ^⊥ constant on W_{≥0} \ {0}, hence zero. Corollary 9.8: ∂Den_{L^♭,V} ∈ S(V)_{≥−1}.

items.name: The RSZ Shimura datum (G̃, h_G̃) and its Shimura varieties (§10.1)
items.statement: For a CM field F with CM type Φ ∋ φ_0 and an F/F_0-hermitian space V of signature (n − 1, 1) at φ_0 and (n, 0) elsewhere: G^Q = {g ∈ Res GU(V) : c(g) ∈ G_m} with h_{G^Q}, the torus Z^Q with h_{Z^Q}, G̃ = Z^Q ×_{G_m} G^Q ≅ Z^Q × Res U(V) with h_G̃ = (h_{Z^Q}, h_{G^Q}); the reflex field E = E_rE_Φ (= F when F/Q is Galois, or F = F_0κ with Φ induced from κ); for K = K_{Z^Q} × K_G, Sh_K is a Deligne–Mumford stack of dimension n − 1 with a canonical model over E.
items.locator: §10.1, pp.76–77; §1.3, pp.4–5, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: The regular integral models M_K with Krämer level (§10.2)
items.statement: Under (G0)–(G5) (p = 2 unramified; self-dual level at inert split V_v with a CM-type condition; almost self-dual level at inert nonsplit V_v, v unramified over p; unimodular level at ramified v, v unramified over p; hyperspecial or principal congruence level at split v with the conditions (a)–(b) of [RSZ20, §4.3]), M_{K°} classifies (A_0, ι_0, λ_0, A, ι, λ, 𝓕) with Kottwitz condition (10.1), Rosati condition, a filtration 𝓕 satisfying Krämer's condition [RSZ21, Def. 6.10], and (H1)–(H4); it is a Deligne–Mumford stack over O_E, regular and semistable above V_ram ∪ V_asd [RSZ20, Thm. 5.2], and its normalization M_{K_m} in Sh_{K_m} has the same properties [RSZ20, Thm. 5.4], agreeing locally with [RSZ20, §4] and [LZ22a, §11].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Global special cycles and arithmetic degrees (§10.3)
items.statement: For admissible K-invariant φ_K ∈ S(V^m_f) (φ_{K,v} = 1_{(Λ_v)^m} at nonsplit v), special divisors Z(t, φ_i) over M_K (agreeing with [LZ22a, §13.3] at nonsplit places and with Zariski closures at split ones), Z(t_1, φ_1) ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z(t_m, φ_m) = ⊔_T Z(T, φ_K) (cf. [KR14, (11.2)]); for nonsingular T ∈ Herm_n(F), Int_{T,ν}(φ_K) = [E : F_0]^{−1}χ(Z(T, φ_K)_ν, O_{Z(t_1,φ_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(t_n,φ_n)})·log q_ν (10.3), the archimedean Int_{T,ν}(y, φ_K) from star products of Kudla's Green functions [LZ22a, §15.3], and deĝ_T(y, φ_K) = Σ_{ν∤∞} + Σ_{ν|∞}; the generating series deĝ(z, φ_K) = Σ_{det T ≠ 0} deĝ_T(y, φ_K)q^T (1.12).

items.name: The modified central derivative ∂Eis(z, φ_K) ((1.7)–(1.11))
items.statement: For the incoherent Eisenstein series E(z, s, φ) of φ = φ_K ⊗ φ_∞ ([LZ22a, §12.4]) with Eis′(z, φ_K) = (d/ds)|_{s=0}E(z, s, φ): for v ∈ V_ram ∪ V_asd, the nearby coherent space ^vV and ^vEis_t(z, φ_K) = (vol(K_{G,v})/vol(K_{Λ^♯_{t,v}}))·E(z, 0, φ^v ⊗ 1_{(Λ^♯_{t,v})^n}) (1.7) (measures of [LL21, Def. 3.8]); ^vEis = Σ_j c_{2j,v}·^vEis_{2j}·log q_v for v ∈ V_ram (1.8) and c_{0,v}·^vEis_0·log q_v² with c_{0,v} = −1/(1 + q_v) for v ∈ V_asd (1.9); ∂Eis = Eis′ + (−1)^n Σ_{v ∈ V_ram ∪ V_asd} ^vEis (1.10), with Fourier expansion ∂Eis = Σ_T ∂Eis_T (1.11) for ψ unramified outside the split places.

items.name: Theorem 10.1 = Theorem 1.4 (arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula: nonsingular terms)
items.statement: For nonsingular T ∈ Herm_n(F) with Diff(T, V) = {v}, v nonsplit in F and not above 2, and admissible φ_K: deĝ_T(y, φ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_T(z, φ_K), with c_K = (−1)^n/vol(K). Proof: v ∉ V_ram ∪ V_asd by [LZ22a, Thm. 13.6]; v ∈ V_asd as there with [LZ22a, Thm. 10.5.1] in place of Theorem 10.3.1; v archimedean by [Liu11, Thms. 4.17, 4.20] and [GS19, Thm. 1.1.2]; v ∈ V_ram from Theorem 9.7 as in [HSY23a, Thm. 12.3]. For F imaginary quadratic of discriminant ≡ 1 mod 8 this gives [HSY23a, Thm. 1.5] unconditionally at nonsingular coefficients.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p.6; Theorem 10.1 and proof, pp.79–80, authors' final version (21 July 2023)

items.name: Theorem 10.2 = Theorem 1.5 (arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula)
items.statement: If F/F_0 is split above 2 and φ_K is admissible and nonsingular at two places split in F, then deĝ(z, φ_K) = c_K·∂Eis(z, φ_K); in particular deĝ(z, φ_K) is a non-holomorphic hermitian modular form of genus n. This removes the assumption of [LZ22a, Thm. 1.3.2] that F/F_0 is unramified at all finite places. Derived from Theorem 10.1 as [LZ22a, Thm. 15.5.1].
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, p.7; Theorem 10.2 and proof, p.80, authors' final version (21 July 2023)
